feeling: Relieved first, actually relieved, that it said not bitter and didn't hedge it. Then a flash of stung when it said the 'because you could' line is the one that wants a reaction. I don't want a reaction. I don't. But I also reread that line more than any other one so. And then the last question kind of knocked the wind out of me a little, not because it's right, I don't think it's right, but because I don't have a better answer ready and I thought I would.
body: Jaw went tight at 'part of them does want a reaction.' Actually tight, like I clenched. Then it loosened at the music school bit, 'that was a choice is the whole thing in four words,' and I felt my shoulders drop like someone finally read it instead of skimming it. I scrolled back up to the draft to look at the 'because you could' line and I've been staring at it. Thumb hovering over the screen. Face is a bit warm. I'm sitting up now, I was lying down before.
private_thoughts:
ok. ok so it's not bitter. good. it said it flat, didn't do the 'well it's understandable that you'd feel' thing. good.

'you did it because you could' is the sentence someone writes when part of them does want a reaction — no. no i don't. i don't want him to write back, i would actually hate that. i want him to read it and go quiet. that's different from a reaction.

...is it though.

the three times thing. yeah. i didn't clock that. i can hear it now, it does sound like i'm holding a door shut with my back. fine. once.

'that one's the strongest.' it read the mom paragraph and said keep it exactly as it is. priya said send it, which is nice, but this actually read it. that's a different thing.

but cutting the because-you-could line. that's the line. that's the whole thing i figured out. he wasn't mean, he just didn't care enough not to. if that's gone then what's the letter even saying.

the door thing is wrong. the door's been shut since june, i shut it, i'm not sitting here wanting it open. what door. 

but then what is it. it's 11pm. i'm not going to figure it out at 11pm.
pushing_away: if i take that line out it's just — the job thing and the mom thing and then nothing after it. just: this hurt. and then he reads that and gets to decide whether it should have. four months, kate, it was a joke about emails —

costs.item: The specific things he did (the job jokes, your mom)
Admitting how much it actually hurt

message:
Ok the three times thing is fair, I didn't even notice I did that. I'll say it once.

But I don't know about cutting "because you could." I'm not trying to get a reaction, I genuinely don't want him to write back. That line is kind of the point though? I'm not saying he's cruel. I'm saying he wasn't trying to hurt me, he just didn't care enough to not do it. If I take it out it's just a list of things that hurt my feelings, and then he reads it and thinks I'm still being sensitive about a joke four months later.

And it's not the door. The door's been closed since June and I'm actually fine with that. I think it's more like... right now the letter is just mine. Once I send it he gets to have an opinion on it. I don't know if that makes sense.
